reality_delta: Cap added a three-track lifecycle gate (architecture, governance, contracts) to development_lifecycle.py and claims all self-checks pass. However, the evidence pattern is consistent with a gate that checks for the presence of review track labels (i.e., the packet must contain objects named "architecture", "governance", "contracts") rather than validating the substance of those reviews. The self-checks — lifecycle self-check, archaeology check, phase2-blueprint check, redcap check — all "passed after implementation," which is the exact pattern of tests that prove the checker exists but don't prove the checker rejects invalid input. No negative test evidence was provided. Additionally, the enforcement-matrix.json was modified (visible in git status) but omitted from the changed_reality list — an undisclosed scope change. The phase2_blueprint change allowing "all-verified" queue state conveniently enables declaring Phase 2 complete, but its necessity to the lifecycle review task is unclear. The user's reality may have changed only in ceremony — packets now declare review tracks — without substantive enforcement that catches real problems.
main_concern: The review_tracks gate may check presence of labels (architecture/governance/contracts objects exist in the packet) without validating the quality, evidence, or reasoning within those reviews. If the gate only requires the packet to declare "architecture review: done" without checking what the review actually found, then the behavioral change is ceremonial — more paperwork, not more safety. The self-checks passing proves the happy path works (well-formed packets proceed) but the absence of negative test evidence means we don't know if malformed or insufficient-review packets are actually blocked. Ceremonial gates create a false sense of rigor while adding only documentation overhead.
top_risks: Ceremonial gate: review_tracks validates label presence (architecture/governance/contracts exist) but not review substance — packets can declare reviews without evidence of actual review
Undisclosed enforcement-matrix.json modification — this file changed but was omitted from the changed_reality list, indicating either an oversight or an intentional scope leak
Self-check-only verification: all four tests are self-checks that the AI ran and passed — zero third-party or negative-test evidence that the gate catches invalid states
missing_evidence: Negative test: a packet with missing or empty review_tracks being correctly blocked by the lifecycle gate
What changed in enforcement-matrix.json and why it was omitted from the disclosure
Evidence that review_tracks validation checks review substance (evidence presence, reasoning quality, not just label/key existence)
minimum_fix: Provide at least one negative test case demonstrating that the lifecycle gate blocks a transition when review_tracks are missing, empty, or contain substantively insufficient reviews. Disclose and justify the enforcement-matrix.json change. If the gate already performs substance checks, provide the specific validation logic (not just the self-check passing) that demonstrates it rejects weak reviews.
